source.author: verg
source.text: Sic deinde effatus frondenti tempora ramo implicat et geniumque loci primamque deorum Tellurem nymphasque et adhuc ignota precatur flumina, tum Noctem Noctisque orientia signa Idaeumque Iovem Phrygiamque ex ordine matrem invocat et duplicis caeloque ereboque parentis.
source.text_original: Sic deinde effatus frondenti tempora ramo / implicat et geniumque loci primamque deorum / Tellurem nymphasque et adhuc ignota precatur / flumina, tum Noctem Noctisque orientia signa / Idaeumque Iovem Phrygiamque ex ordine matrem / invocat et duplicis caeloque ereboque parentis.
source.text_english: Then speaking thus, he twines his brows with a leafy bough and prays to the Spirit of the Place, to Earth the first of the gods, to the nymphs and the rivers still unknown, then calls on Night and the rising signs of Night and Idaean Iuppiter and the Phrygian Mother in turn, and the parent with two forms, from heaven and from Erebus.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: hunc nouos ritus ac pompas sacrorum introduxisse et primum diis sacrificasse, id estVestae , quae dicitur Tellus, unde poetae: primamque deorum Tellurem et postmodum Deum Matri.
reuse.text_original: hunc nouos ritus ac pompas sacrorum introduxisse et primum diis sacrificasse, id estVestae , quae dicitur Tellus, — unde poetae: primamque deorum Tellurem — et postmodum Deum Matri.
reuse.text_english: that he introduced new rites and pageants of sacred ceremonies and first offered sacrifice to the gods, that is, to Vesta, who is called Tellus; hence the poets say that Tellus was first among the gods and later the Mother of the Gods.
